Si.label: Silicon — diamond / cubic benchmark
Si.note: The first-order silicon mode is the T2g triplet, also called F2g. Three orthogonal partners are summed as intensities. A unity cubic lattice gives the correct (hkl) direction without the absolute lattice length.

profiles.CUBIC_VV: VV: parallel linear states, scan theta
profiles.CUBIC_VH: VH: crossed linear states, scan theta
profiles.LINEAR_PAIR: VV and VH together, one coefficient set
profiles.CIRCULAR_LINEAR: Circular input / direct linear analyzer, scan alpha
profiles.QWP: Input QWP / Raman tensor / return QWP / linear analyzer
profiles.DIRECT_JONES: Custom direct Jones input and detection states

CUBIC_VV.label: VV: parallel linear states, scan theta
CUBIC_VV.detection: Linear analyzer parallel to the input
CUBIC_VV.invariant: The paired VV/VH choice must reproduce this VV channel with identical inputs.
CUBIC_VV.use_for: Parallel linear measurements and the VV member of the cubic benchmark.
CUBIC_VV.caution: Both linear states rotate together in the fixed-tensor coordinates. This represents a sample-angle experiment with a declared sign convention; do not also rotate the tensor by the same scan angle.
CUBIC_VV.provenance: Direct specialization of the cited contraction and linear states.

CUBIC_VH.label: VH: crossed linear states, scan theta
CUBIC_VH.detection: Linear analyzer perpendicular to the input
CUBIC_VH.invariant: The paired VV/VH choice must reproduce this VH channel with identical inputs.
CUBIC_VH.use_for: Crossed linear measurements and the VH member of the cubic benchmark.
CUBIC_VH.caution: Both linear states rotate together in the fixed-tensor coordinates. This represents a sample-angle experiment with a declared sign convention; do not also rotate the tensor by the same scan angle.
CUBIC_VH.provenance: Direct specialization of the cited contraction and crossed states.

LINEAR_PAIR.label: VV and VH together, one coefficient set
LINEAR_PAIR.scan: theta: one common angle for both channels
LINEAR_PAIR.preparation: One linear input and one shared coefficient set
LINEAR_PAIR.detection: Calculate parallel and perpendicular analyzers separately
LINEAR_PAIR.amplitude: \mathcal A_{VV}=v^\dagger R_\perp v,\quad\mathcal A_{VH}=w^\dagger R_\perp v
LINEAR_PAIR.invariant: This is a paired output, not a third polarization law. Each raw curve equals its standalone channel.
LINEAR_PAIR.use_for: Comparing VV and VH for the same phonon coefficients, surface and angular zero.
LINEAR_PAIR.caution: Both linear states rotate together in the fixed-tensor coordinates. This represents a sample-angle experiment with a declared sign convention; do not also rotate the tensor by the same scan angle.
LINEAR_PAIR.provenance: Two instances of the same Jones engine; powers are not added to define a new channel.

CIRCULAR_LINEAR.label: Circular input / direct linear analyzer, scan alpha
CIRCULAR_LINEAR.return_path: Identity: the detector state at the sample is linear
CIRCULAR_LINEAR.detection: v(alpha+alpha0), with a calibrated analyzer zero
CIRCULAR_LINEAR.invariant: For sigma+ input it equals custom Jones with theta_i=45, beta_i=90, theta_s0=alpha0 and beta_s=0 degrees.
CIRCULAR_LINEAR.use_for: Circular illumination with a linear effective detector at the sample.
CIRCULAR_LINEAR.caution: A bare linear-analyzer scan does not select pure sigma+ or sigma- endpoints. A return QWP changes the effective detector.
CIRCULAR_LINEAR.provenance: Program Jones-calculus extension. The circular selection-rule paper does not prescribe this continuous scan or its quantitative intensity.

CUBIC_SIGMA.label: sigma+alpha reference: elliptical detection-state scan
CUBIC_SIGMA.detection: j(pi/4+alpha, pi/2), elliptical except at special angles
CUBIC_SIGMA.invariant: It equals custom Jones at theta_i=45, beta_i=90, theta_s0=45, beta_s=90 degrees; source QWP endpoints agree up to phase, intermediate states generally differ.
CUBIC_SIGMA.use_for: The cubic paper sigma+alpha equations, its Fig. 1(c) benchmark and the declared slide-frame example.
CUBIC_SIGMA.caution: This implements Eq. (11) at theta=pi/4 and beta=beta'=pi/2. The paper calls alpha a polarizer angle, but its effective detector is not a bare linear state at the sample. An apparatus must be calibrated before identifying the two.
CUBIC_SIGMA.provenance: Cited effective Jones parameterization; the p/q expansion is derived here from that state.

QWP.label: Input QWP / Raman tensor / return QWP / linear analyzer
QWP.scan: alpha: physical linear analyzer after the return plate
QWP.preparation: Lab-X input through Q=Rot(-pi/4) diag(1,i) Rot(-pi/4)^T
QWP.return_path: B=Q.T in the uploaded source basis convention
QWP.detection: Linear analyzer (-sin alpha, cos alpha) after B; effective detector B.H times analyzer
QWP.invariant: At alpha=0 and pi/2 the circular endpoints equal the elliptical reference in power; intermediate intensities generally need not match.
QWP.use_for: The uploaded QWP optical sequence, after its axes, return-path convention and analyzer zero are verified.
QWP.caution: Q.T is a declared source convention, not a universal reverse-path rule. Keep either the explicit B or its effective detector, never both. The crystal tensor remains 3x3 before transverse restriction.
QWP.provenance: Exact uploaded optical chain plus a program-derived p/q identity valid for any supplied R_perp under that chain.

CIRCULAR_SAME.label: Same fixed circular basis label
CIRCULAR_SAME.scan: None: both sample states are fixed
CIRCULAR_SAME.invariant: The curve is constant when tensor, orientation and optical states remain fixed; a polar circle is a display of that constant.
CIRCULAR_SAME.use_for: A fixed same-basis circular channel; compare helicity labels only after reconciling beam directions.
CIRCULAR_SAME.caution: Same fixed XY circular label is not automatically conserved propagation-relative helicity in backscattering. This profile does not rotate the sample.
CIRCULAR_SAME.provenance: Fixed-state tensor contraction; the separate angular-momentum rule is conditional and does not set curve heights.

CIRCULAR_OPPOSITE.label: Opposite fixed circular basis label
CIRCULAR_OPPOSITE.scan: None: both sample states are fixed
CIRCULAR_OPPOSITE.invariant: The curve is constant under this fixed experiment. Its power is the opposite-basis circular channel, not an alpha sweep.
CIRCULAR_OPPOSITE.use_for: A fixed opposite-basis circular channel, with an explicit propagation convention.
CIRCULAR_OPPOSITE.caution: Opposite fixed XY circular labels can represent conserved physical helicity for counterpropagating beams. Match the reference's basis before assigning conserved/changing names.
CIRCULAR_OPPOSITE.provenance: Fixed-state tensor contraction, distinct from a spatial vortex-intensity calculation.

DIRECT_JONES.label: Custom direct Jones input and detection states
DIRECT_JONES.scan: alpha: theta_s0+alpha; input and phase controls fixed
DIRECT_JONES.return_path: Identity: any return optics must already be included in e_s
DIRECT_JONES.invariant: It reproduces a preset only when both effective states and their scan laws agree up to global phase; an arbitrary waveplate path need not fit this restricted constant-beta scan.
DIRECT_JONES.use_for: Calibrated effective states or exact checks of the matching preset parameters.
DIRECT_JONES.caution: Changing beta_s changes relative phase and interference. This custom profile keeps the input fixed, so it does not in general reproduce co-rotating VV/VH scans.
DIRECT_JONES.provenance: User-defined specialization of the common contraction, not a separate material law.

config.case_label: Ag components on the (211) reference frame
config.input_note: Unity metric reproduces the slide XY convention. Enter actual lattice ratios for a physical tilted CaNb2O6 surface.
Symmetry-allowed full 3×3 D2h tensors and unchanged Quarter-wave-plate optics. Coefficients are illustrative. The principal (100) orientation does not require an assumed tilted-surface lattice ratio.
Main calculation of the supplied Quarter-wave-plate notebook; a=1, A=0.4, delta=phi=60 degrees is an illustrative source example.

config.case_label: Complex linear model BP: Fig. 5 ratios, Eq. 13 scans
config.input_note: Fig. 5 prints c/a=1.96 and phi_ac=0 degrees for Ag(1), c/a=1.32 and phi_ac=94 degrees for Ag(2), and an off-diagonal reference magnitude 1.30. a=1 fixes an arbitrary scale for each illustrative branch. Curves reproduce Eq. 13 with the displayed angle zero, not digitized experimental data.
D3h plane-wave Jones tensors and circular channels; the alpha scan is a direct Jones extension. Intensities use illustrative coefficients, not a prediction of the vortex paper.
Si T2g triplet; paper Eq. 4 axes, Eq. 11 states, common d; theoretical matrix calculation.

validation_procedures.title: Circular-basis orthonormality
validation_procedures.purpose: Exclude incorrect normalization and missing complex conjugation.
validation_procedures.procedure: Form the Gram matrix of the two circular vectors.

validation_procedures.title: Explicit quarter-wave-plate matrix
validation_procedures.purpose: Detect an axis-angle or retardance sign error before scattering.
validation_procedures.procedure: Compare the implemented plate with the matrix printed in the source.

validation_procedures.title: Lossless and symmetric plate
validation_procedures.purpose: Check norm preservation by this ideal plate and its symmetry in the adopted basis.
validation_procedures.procedure: Compute Q dagger Q and Q transpose. This is not a unitarity requirement on the Raman tensor.

validation_procedures.title: Incident circular state
validation_procedures.purpose: Confirm the selected plate actually prepares the intended incident state.
validation_procedures.procedure: Propagate x-polarized input and compare vectors including the unit global phase.

validation_procedures.title: General circular amplitudes
validation_procedures.purpose: Check the output-input index order and the signs of all Cartesian entries.
validation_procedures.procedure: Contract a general complex 2x2 tensor and compare independent entry formulas.

validation_procedures.title: Modified source tensor
validation_procedures.purpose: Verify the extra yy phase and the cancellation of antisymmetric off-diagonal entries in the flipped channel.
validation_procedures.procedure: Substitute the source tensor into the circular contractions.

validation_procedures.title: Scattered-field reconstruction
validation_procedures.purpose: Ensure no circular amplitude is lost before return propagation.
validation_procedures.procedure: Compare Cartesian scattering with its complete circular expansion.

validation_procedures.title: Return plate and physical angle zero
validation_procedures.purpose: Detect a wrong return matrix or an arbitrary analyzer reference that would rotate or mirror a plot.
validation_procedures.procedure: Reconstruct the two returned circular states, their real axes and their relative phase.

validation_procedures.title: Analyzer endpoint calibration
validation_procedures.purpose: Establish what alpha=0 and alpha=90 degrees detect in this optical chain.
validation_procedures.procedure: Transmit each returned circular state through both calibrated analyzer endpoints.

validation_procedures.title: Matrix chain versus circular amplitude
validation_procedures.purpose: Check matrix ordering and the relative phase that sets the interference sign.
validation_procedures.procedure: Compare the production amplitude with the independent circular-channel expansion.

validation_procedures.title: Three intensity pieces
validation_procedures.purpose: Identify an incorrect complex conjugate or an incorrect sign in the interference term.
validation_procedures.procedure: Independently evaluate the two powers and Im(R++ R-+ conjugate).

validation_procedures.title: Symbolic squared-modulus identity
validation_procedures.purpose: Prove the hand formula agrees with the matrix result without inserting it into the plotting engine.
validation_procedures.procedure: Reduce the symbolic difference between A times A conjugate and the source closed form to zero.

validation_procedures.title: Seeded numerical intensity comparison
validation_procedures.purpose: Cross-check symbolic processing against independent complex NumPy propagation.
validation_procedures.procedure: Repeat the source's four seed-1 parameter samples, then 64 phase/sign/zero cases.

validation_procedures.title: Fourier reconstruction
validation_procedures.purpose: Check the harmonic representation used to determine continuous extrema.
validation_procedures.procedure: Reconstruct the intensity from independently derived constant, cosine and sine coefficients.

validation_procedures.title: Old-tensor limit
validation_procedures.purpose: Recover the earlier model when the new relative yy phase vanishes.
validation_procedures.procedure: Set phi=0 and compare the complete angular law, not only one angle.

validation_procedures.title: Diagonal-tensor phase limit
validation_procedures.purpose: Check that a relative diagonal phase shifts the analyzer pattern with the correct sign.
validation_procedures.procedure: Set A=0 and compare with the independently shifted cosine law.

validation_procedures.title: Pure flipped-channel limit
validation_procedures.purpose: Confirm extinction of the same-label channel in a known limiting tensor.
validation_procedures.procedure: Set A=0 and phi=pi.

validation_procedures.title: All four circular channels
validation_procedures.purpose: Check both input labels and prevent interchange of incident and detected indices.
validation_procedures.procedure: Derive all four circular amplitudes and compare their squared moduli with the source formulas.

validation_procedures.title: Four channels through real optical chains
validation_procedures.purpose: Validate the physical preparation and detection path rather than relying only on a basis transform.
validation_procedures.procedure: Prepare each input with its own +/-45-degree plate and compare same/flip endpoint powers; use the source's five seed-5 samples plus a zero case.

validation_procedures.title: Circular-input difference and dissymmetry
validation_procedures.purpose: Check the source's contrast definition and its denominator; do not infer material chirality from this algebraic test.
validation_procedures.procedure: Subtract complete powers for the two incident labels and compare the analytic difference.

validation_procedures.title: Zero-contrast limits
validation_procedures.purpose: Detect a spurious circular-input difference in limiting cases where it must vanish.
validation_procedures.procedure: Substitute A=0, phi=pi and delta=phi/2 separately into the computed difference.

validation_procedures.title: Alternative-convention mirror check
validation_procedures.purpose: Identify a documented change of optical convention without forcing different experiments to share one curve.
validation_procedures.procedure: Use the appendix return plate and lab-x analyzer, then compare with the main source law at -alpha.
validation_procedures.expected_latex: I_{\rm appendix}(\alpha)=I_{\rm main}(-\alpha)\quad\text{for the declared source tensor}

validation_procedures.title: Angular periodicity
validation_procedures.purpose: Ensure that the plotted first-harmonic amplitude gives a 180-degree intensity period.
validation_procedures.procedure: Translate the source scan by pi and reduce the difference symbolically.

validation_procedures.title: Dark source and undefined contrast
validation_procedures.purpose: Avoid reporting a finite dissymmetry for a completely dark source.
validation_procedures.procedure: Set a=A=0 and require all powers to vanish while CID is explicitly undefined.

validation_procedures.title: Deliberately incorrect controls
validation_procedures.purpose: Demonstrate that the checker can detect conjugation, interference-sign and intensity errors.
validation_procedures.procedure: Require rejection of three injected mistakes at declared nontrivial parameters.

validation_source.notation: R[out,in]: first index = detected circular label; second = incident label.
validation_source.scope: The source is an effective complex 2x2 optical model. Its antisymmetric off-diagonal pair is not substituted for a D2h material tensor.
